extracted.intended_audience: attorneys practicing before the USPTO, respondents in OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO/OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order from the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline resolving a disciplinary complaint by stipulation; sets forth jurisdictional bases, stipulated facts, legal conclusion (violation of USPTO ethics rule), and a package of sanctions, reporting, and enforcement procedures. Useful as a template of procedural requirements and sanction conditions in USPTO disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the statutory and regulatory bases for OED jurisdiction to investigate and discipline non-patent and patent practitioners who practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to practice non-patent matters before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney licensed and in good standing in a State may be authorized to practice before the USPTO in trademark or other non-patent cases and matters pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being authorized to represent others before the USPTO in non-patent matters subjects an attorney to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Disciplinary Rules even if not a registered patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: state disciplinary suspension triggers USPTO rule (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct resulting in discipline by a duly constituted authority of a State can violate 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) and form the basis for USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent's disciplinary action in a state bar (e.g., suspension on ethical grounds) may be sufficient for the OED to conclude a violation of USPTO ethics regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited conduct per California Rule 3-310(E): conflicts without informed written consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting representation adverse to a former client, representing more than one client in a matter in which the interests of the clients actually conflicted without the informed written consent of each client, violates California Rule of Professional Conduct 3-310(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-bar findings of conflict-of-interest violations are relevant facts for USPTO disciplinary determinations when they involve ethical misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be publicly reprimanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reprimand is an express sanction ordered by the USPTO and is to be published as set forth in the order (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary term
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a thirty-six month (three year) period of probation commencing on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation conditions are enforceable for the specified period and tied to other remedial and reporting obligations in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice during probation conditioned on compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be permitted to practice trademark and non-patent law before the USPTO during her probationary period unless suspended by order of the USPTO Director and provided that she otherwise satisfies the conditions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission to continue non-patent practice is conditional and may be revoked if probation terms or disciplinary rules are violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend Respondent for up to twenty-four months; (2) the Order to Show Cause shall be sent to Respondent at the address of record and Respondent shall be granted fifteen days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the initial procedural step and a 15-day response period when OED suspects non-compliance during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation to USPTO Director and request for immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the 15-day response period and consideration of any response, the OED Director continues to conclude Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response if any, and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the OED Director's conclusion, and shall request the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to twenty-four months for the violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the evidentiary and transmission requirements for the OED Director's request for immediate suspension to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate suspension consequences: dissociation of USPTO accounts and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order immediately suspending Respondent, then (i) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates; (ii) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until she is reinstated; and (iii) Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until she is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate suspension includes technical/accounting measures to prevent access/use of USPTO filing and authentication systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of suspension does not stay effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of the USPTO Director's immediate suspension, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or other review processes do not automatically stay an immediate suspension ordered by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may pursue further disciplinary proceedings under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent in accordance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused Respondent to be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not preclude independent or additional disciplinary proceedings based on the same misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at: http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public posting is required as part of the sanction and transparency obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice in the Official Gazette with material content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation' in the Official Gazette stating that Respondent has been publicly reprimanded and placed on probation for three years for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6), summarizing the California suspension and basis for discipline, and noting Respondent is not a registered patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must convey key facts of the discipline, the statutory/regulatory bases, and respondent's authorization status before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates cross-notification to state bar authorities and courts as part of reciprocal and public notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification obligation within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, within thirty days from the date this Final Order is signed, shall notify all clients who have a trademark case(s) pending before the Office on the date this Final Order is signed, if any, of her probation by providing each such client a copy of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires affirmative outreach to current USPTO clients in trademark matters so they are informed of the practitioner's disciplinary status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance or statement of no clients within 45 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, within forty-five days from the date this Final Order is signed, shall either (i) provide the OED Director with an affidavit attesting to her compliance with the client-notification obligation and evidence of compliance (copies of the correspondence sent), or (ii) provide an affidavit attesting that she had no clients who had trademark case(s) pending before the Office on the date the Final Order was signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a verification and documentary-evidence requirement to demonstrate compliance with the client-notification obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record may be considered in future proceedings as aggravating factor or to rebut representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary findings and orders may be used against the respondent in subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No award of costs between the parties as part of the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of reciprocal disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The reciprocal disciplinary proceeding pending against Respondent is hereby dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement resolves and dismisses the reciprocal matter as specified in the agreement.
